connector: What does a good paragraph about a character need? A pillar, a real example from the book, and a sentence that says what it shows. Today you write two of them.

a.raw: jemmys courage grew slowly throughout the whipping boy and by the end he had become someone even he didnt recognize
a.fixed: Jemmy’s courage grew slowly throughout The Whipping Boy, and by the end he had become someone even he didn’t recognize.
a.why: Jemmy’s shows belonging. A book title gets capitals. A comma goes before and. Didn’t joins did and not.

b.raw: despereauxs courage grew in the dark and by the end he had saved the princess
b.fixed: Despereaux’s courage grew in the dark, and by the end he had saved the princess.
b.why: Despereaux’s shows belonging, so it gets a capital and an apostrophe. A comma goes before and.

cards.title: World Notes: Real Whipping Boys?
cards.sub: A real thing behind one of our books
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: The Whipping Boy is a made-up story, but it grew from an old idea: a boy who was punished when a prince misbehaved.
Prince Edward of England, who later became King Edward VI, grew up with a best friend named Barnaby Fitzpatrick. Stories say Barnaby was Edward’s whipping boy.

Historians today say there is no proof from that time that Barnaby was ever whipped for the prince. But he really was the prince’s closest friend, a little like Jemmy and Prince Brat at the end of the book.

notes.wordParts: Word parts I know: -y and -ness mean being something, -ous means full of, -ful means full of, -less means without, un- means not, re- means again.
notes.grammar: Editing checklist: capitals on names and the first word, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, a comma before and/but/so when it joins two complete thoughts, and the right past form, like went.
notes.spelling: Find the base word first. Then check what was added: drop the silent e (hope, hoping), double the last letter (hop, hopping), change y to i (cry, cried), or add -es (box, boxes).
notes.wgrd: A body paragraph names one pillar, gives a real example from the book, and says what the example shows about the character.
vocab: doing the right thing even when no one is watching
understanding and sharing the feelings of another person
the ability to keep going after something hard
continuing to try even when things are hard

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: Let's try all three parts with a different sentence, from The Tale of Despereaux. Nothing is sweeter in this sad world than the sound of someone you love calling your name. Nothing. Part one, read like a reader. The princess calls Despereaux's name, and it means everything to him. Part two, read like a writer. The author stops, then adds one more word: Nothing. The add-on makes us stop and feel it. Part three, write your own. My turn: Pizza night is the best night of the week. The best. Now it's your turn with Mrs. Lambchop's sentence. Write one sentence in each box.

items.t: Jemmy orders the outlaws, “Lay down the whip,” to stop them from whipping the prince. (The Whipping Boy)
items.why: Courage: he speaks up even though the outlaws are dangerous.

items.t: When the outlaws whip Prince Brat, he sets his jaw and does not make a sound. (The Whipping Boy)
items.why: Courage: he is brave, just the way Jemmy always was.

items.t: People make fun of Stanley and call him names because he is flat. (Flat Stanley)
items.why: Calling names is not respect. Mrs. Lambchop says it is wrong to dislike people for their shapes.
